Q: Is it possible to use ControlValueAccessor to bind a FormArray to a custom component in Angular? A:

what version of Angular?

In the last ones, you use

   FormGroup({
          id: new FormControl(dto?.id),
          ...
          items: new FormArray<FormGroup>( //<--see that you indicate 
                                           //   is a FormArray of FormGroup
           ....
          )
        })

BTW, you can use a simple component with viewProviders if your component are only a serie of "inputs"

viewProviders:[{ provide: ControlContainer, useExisting: FormGroupDirective }]

see this old SO

Q: Explanation of output of Python tqdm. A:

tqdm maintainer here :)

This is explained by (and customisable via) the bar_format keyword argument. You can print
the help using:

  • pydoc tqdm.tqdm

  • tqdm --help

  • https://tqdm.github.io/docs/tqdm/

bar_format  : str, optional
    Specify a custom bar string formatting. May impact performance.
    [default: '{l_bar}{bar}{r_bar}'], where
    l_bar='{desc}: {percentage:3.0f}%|' and
    r_bar='| {n_fmt}/{total_fmt} [{elapsed}<{remaining}, {rate_fmt}{postfix}]'
    Possible vars: l_bar, bar, r_bar, n, n_fmt, total, total_fmt,
        percentage, elapsed, elapsed_s, ncols, nrows, desc, unit,
        rate, rate_fmt, rate_noinv, rate_noinv_fmt,
        rate_inv, rate_inv_fmt, postfix, unit_divisor,
        remaining, remaining_s, eta.
    Note that a trailing ": " is automatically removed after {desc}
    if the latter is empty.

Q: How to get raw mouse XY data in VB6 A:

Note: The solution to my question in this answer is based on the very helpful comments of [/u/GSerg](https://stackoverflow.com/users/11683/gserg)

Also note the option was considered to use DirectX. But according to wikipedia: "DirectInput: Input API (for interfacing with keyboards, mice, joysticks, and game controllers ) was deprecated after version 8 in favor of (Xinput for Xbox controllers or) standard WM_INPUT window message processing for keyboard and mouse input)". This microsoft article [taking advantage of high-dpi mouse movement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dxtecharts/taking-advantage-of-high-dpi-mouse-movement) also refers.

This Answer focuses on the problem areas in the Question.

An alternative form of Answer would provide a full set of VB6 code. The MS document "Using Raw Input" linked below provides a code sample in C showing the 'minimal pattern' for standard reading raw input from a WM_INPUT message handler.

Here are some (of many) Microsoft documents (focused on C and C++, not VB6) relating to the methods used:-

[Using Raw Input](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/using-raw-input?source=recommendations)

[Raw Input](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/raw-input?source=recommendations)

[RAWINPUT structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-rawinput)

[RAWINPUTHEADER structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-rawinputheader)

[RAWMOUSE structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-rawmouse)

The first issue is to correct the parameters in the First call to GetRawInputData putting ByVal 0& instead of vbNullString and setting cbSizeHeader=16 (the standard length of theRAWINPUTHEADER ).

cbSizeHeader=16
status = GetRawInputData(lParam, uiCommand, ByVal 0&, pcbSize, cbSizeHeader)

This will return the the value of 40(bytes) for pcbsize .

Then the pData array to receive the mouse data should be sized to 40 bytes,

Then in the second call to GetRawInputData the third parameter will be pData(0).

status = GetRawInputData(lParam, uiCommand, pData(0), pcbSize, cbSizeHeader)

The UDT type structure to receive the header and mouse data should be something like:-

'in Module...

Public Type RAWINPUTWITHMOUSEDATA
    '------- header ---------
    dwType As Long
    dwSize As Long
    hDevice As Long
    wParam As Long 
    '-------- mouse data--------
    usFlags As Integer
    dummy As Integer'... to ensure correct memory alignment
    '-------------------------
    '... either 1 item:-
    'ulButtons As Long
    '... or 2 items:-
    usButtonFlags As Integer
    usButtonData As Integer
    '-------------------------
    ulRawButtons As Long
    lLastX As Long
    lLastY As Long
    ulExtraInformation As Long
End Type

' in Form code...
dim mouseData as RAWINPUTWITHMOUSEDATA

Then the data can be memory-copied to the mouseData object.

            
'in Module...

Public Declare Sub CopyMemory Lib "kernel32" Alias "RtlMoveMemory" ( _
    ByRef Destination As Any, _
    ByRef Source As Any, _
    ByVal Length As Long)

'in Form code...

CopyMemory mouseData, pData(0), Len(mouseData) '..  Destination, Source, Length

Then the latest mouse position data can be accessed as mouseData.lLastX and mouseData.lLastY.

Note that instead of using copyMemory , the Second call to GetRawInputData can pass the mouse data directly to the mouseData array, thus:-

status = GetRawInputData(lParam, uiCommand, mouseData(0), pcbSize, cbSizeHeader)

Padding

Note that my original UDT Type RAWINPUTWITHMOUSEDATA used 38 bytes, in contrast to the 40 bytes for pcbsize returned by the First call to GetRawInputData .

[\u\Gserg commented here](How to get raw mouse XY data in VB6) suggested putting a dummy As Integer field after usFlags As Integer if sensible values are required for usButtonFlags and usButtonData.

The difference was due to 2 extra bytes of padding being used (by Windows) in the latter to comply with memory alignment padding and packing rules.

This seems to produce acceptable data but I havent checked the mouse button values in detail.

Note on Draining with GetRawInputBuffer

I started looking at using this function in the two ways described in the document [Using Raw Input](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/using-raw-input?source=recommendations) . But I did not get as far as making it work in VB6 . Even if I had managed to drain some RAWINPUT objects into an array ...the macro NEXTRAWINPUTBLOCK is apparently not available to VB6 so there'd be a problem in extracting the mouse data for further processing.

Q: Git LFS storage issue A:

How can I completely remove Git LFS without rewriting history?

I’m currently working on an e-commerce website selling diamond rings and jewellery, and I’m having a problem removing Git LFS from the repository.

Git LFS was originally enabled because the site contains a lot of high-resolution product photography. The diamond ring images can be fairly large, so using LFS seemed like a sensible solution at the time. However, it’s now causing problems with the way I want to deploy and manage the site, so I’d like to remove Git LFS completely and go back to tracking the files normally.

I’ve already tried:

```bash

git lfs uninstall

```

But from what I understand, this only removes the LFS hooks and filter configuration. It doesn’t actually restore the existing LFS-tracked product images as normal Git files.

I can still see the affected files with:

```bash

git lfs ls-files

```

I’ve read that I may need to change `.gitattributes` and then re-index each affected file using something like:

```bash

git rm --cached <file>

git add <file>

```

The problem is that I’m not sure what order these steps should be done in, and I really don’t want to risk losing hundreds of product images or breaking the repository.

I’m also **not looking to rewrite the Git history**. I don’t mind if older commits still use LFS. I just want the current product images and all future files to be tracked by normal Git.

What is the safest way to convert the existing LFS files back to regular Git files, remove LFS from the project, and make sure it doesn’t start tracking the product images again? We are a small team, at Walsh & Partners, any advice, we would be grateful.
